subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: When a Codex approval request expects a native relay but relay invocation fails, which failures may use normal before-tool policy instead of failing closed?
rationale: The generic hook path does not establish that every relay-owned enforcement invariant was applied, and current main deliberately distinguishes failures before and after relay invocation; choosing a permanent fallback boundary requires explicit security ownership.

options.title: Repair lifecycle, preserve fail-closed
options.body: Refresh or reissue the relay generation at its lifecycle owner and retain fail-closed handling after invocation begins.

options.title: Allow guarded pre-invocation fallback
options.body: Permit fallback only for explicitly classified relay-unavailability errors when no invocation was recorded, with live enforcement proof.

options.title: Accept broad generic fallback
options.body: Allow all invocation exceptions to rerun generic policy evaluation and explicitly own the weaker relay-specific boundary.

recommendation.title: Repair lifecycle, preserve fail-closed
recommendation.body: Refresh or reissue the relay generation at its lifecycle owner and retain fail-closed handling after invocation begins.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged both the current guarded unavailable behavior and the restart-generation preservation path that define the decision surface.
